english.title: Fail to permit inspection of snare every day - England
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having knowingly permitted to be set in position in England a snare which was of such a nature and so placed as to be calculated to cause bodily injury to any wild animal coming into contact with it, failed, without reasonable excuse, to inspect it or cause it to be inspected at least once every day that it remained in position
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(3) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) From the 17th October 2023, section 48 of the Agriculture (Wales) Act 2023 amends section 11 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981. This offence applies in England. For the offence applying in Wales and England before this date, see H4679.
(ii) See section 21(7) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(iii) See section 11(5) for presumption that animal is wild and section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(vi) See section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant, having knowingly permitted to be set in position in England a snare which was of such a nature and so placed as to be calculated to cause bodily injury to any wild animal coming into contact with it, failed, without reasonable excuse, to inspect it or cause it to be inspected at least once every day that it remained in position.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 20 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
